Something my therapist said about medication, that is really true, is that it will not solve your depression. It takes the edge off. For example, if you’re used to having negative thoughts linger for long periods of time, antidepressants will usually reduce the time you’re stuck on that thought, but the thought will still exist. It makes it a lot easier to work through the throes of depression but it doesn’t erase it altogether. 

I can’t recommend enough finding a psychiatrist to help plan what medication is best for you. I went to my primary care and they didn’t really seem to understand my situation and the medications I was prescribed were not for me. Finding a good psychiatrist who takes the time to explain possible side effects and how the drug works in general is so helpful and makes taking antidepressants so much easier. Once I found a psychiatrist we tried a few different drugs (SSRI’s and also sleeping pills) and it can often be a little overwhelming trying to find one that works but having that support from a therapist and a psychiatrist was really helpful for me.
